sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 26.0% a year from $4,319 million in FY2016 to $34,639 million in FY2025 [F1][F10][F231].
The path was two step changes rather than a straight line: revenue rose 68.3% in FY2021 and 43.6% in FY2022, then fell 3.9% in FY2023 before recovering 13.7% and 34.3% [D258][D314][D370][D426][D483].
The FY2022 jump included the Xilinx acquisition, which added embedded product revenue for a full year versus a partial period in FY2021 [P35][P41].
FY2025 growth came from Data Center and Client and Gaming, partly offset by a 3% decline in Embedded [P15].
Data Center was 48.0% of FY2025 revenue at $16,635 million and contributed 15.7pp of the 34.3% growth [D692][S98][D694][D483].
That segment grew 32% on strong demand for EPYC processors and Instinct GPU accelerators [P13][D693].
Client and Gaming added 19.0pp, with Client up 51% on a 31% unit increase and 15% higher processor prices [D701][P10].
Operating income grew 94.4% against 34.3% revenue growth, an incremental margin of 20.3% [D484][D483][D511].
Diluted EPS rose 165.0% against 164.2% net income growth, as the diluted share count was flat at -0.1% [D487][D485][D506].
Gross margin of 49.5% is the window high against a 44.7% median, while operating margin of 10.7% sits above its 7.2% median but far below the 22.2% FY2021 high [F40][D800][D801][F60][D795][D794].
The FY2025 gross margin gain of 0.2pp came from product mix, partly offset by about $440 million of MI308 export-control inventory charges [D498][P14].
Operating margin rose 3.3pp, with cost of revenue adding 0.2pp, R&D 1.7pp and SG&A subtracting 1.2pp [D499][D513][D514][D515].
The FY2022 operating margin fell 16.8pp, driven by a 3.3pp cost-of-revenue drag and an 8.5pp residual from acquisition-related amortization [D330][D343][D346][P46].
Net margin of 12.5% exceeded operating margin by 1.9pp, helped by $577 million of other income from unrealized investment gains and a tax benefit [F80][F60][D843][P5][P4].
Operating cash flow of $7,709 million was 1.78x net income and free cash flow of $6,735 million was 1.55x, against a 1.17x window median for free cash flow [F110][F70][D470][F130][D810].
The FY2025 operating inflow reflected $4.3 billion of net income plus $4.6 billion of non-cash adjustments, partly offset by a $2.2 billion inventory build for Data Center ramps [P3].
Free cash flow margin of 19.4% matches the FY2021 high of 19.6%, while capex at 2.8% of revenue ran 1.87x D&A [D467][D803][D466][D472].
Net cash reached $6,456 million in FY2025, 18.6% of revenue, from $3,411 million a year earlier [D476][D477][D419].
That net cash position ranks at the 100th percentile of five semis peers, whose median is -17.3% of revenue [D844][D845].
Total debt rose 138.0% to $4,096 million on $1.5 billion of new notes issued in March 2025 [D508][D475][P6].
Buybacks of $1,316 million were 19.5% of free cash flow, and the diluted share count fell 0.1% [D478][D479][D506].
Revenue fell 3.9% in FY2023 as Client dropped 25% on weak PC demand and inventory correction, partly offset by Embedded [D370][P35].
Total debt rose 138.0% in FY2025 to $4,096 million, though net cash still rose to $6,456 million [D508][D475][D476].
Days inventory outstanding climbed to 165 days from 160, extending a rise from 106 days in FY2022 [D481][D424][D312].
The effective tax rate moved -21.3pp to -2.5% on an $853 million uncertain-tax-position release, so the FY2025 net margin is not a clean run rate [D469][D412][P4].
Whether operating margin holds above the 7.2% window median or slips toward the 1.8% FY2023 level will show if the FY2025 leverage persists [D795][F58].
Days inventory outstanding above the FY2025 level of 165 days would signal the Data Center build is outrunning demand [D481].
Data Center growth below the FY2025 rate of 32.2% would mark a reversal in the segment carrying 48.0% of revenue [D693][D692].
